figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1 | Drugs developed from microbial specialized metabolites since the turn 
of the century.  a | Daptomycin, which is produced by Streptomyces roseosporus, was 
developed to tackle the emerging threat posed by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus 
aureus (MRSA) and other multidrug-resistant Gram-positive pathogenic bacteria. 
b | Fidaxomicin, which is produced by the actinobacterium Dactylosporangium 
aurantiacum subsp. hamdenensis, was introduced to treat life-threatening gastrointestinal 
infections caused by Clostridium difficile. c | Carfilzomib, a synthetic analogue of epoxomicin 
from the bacterium Goodfellowiella coeruleoviolacea, was developed as a chemotherapeutic 
for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, a type of bone marrow cancer.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2 | The genome mining approach for natural product discovery in microorganisms.  Following the 
identification and growth of a microorganism of interest, the genome sequence is obtained. Bioinformatics tools are then 
used to analyse the genome and identify cryptic biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). Silent BGCs are activated using one or 
a combination of pleiotropic or pathway-specific approaches (examples of each are illustrated). Novel metabolites are 
identified in culture extracts or supernatants, followed by their purification and characterization, typically using a 
combination of high-resolution mass spectrometry, and 1D and 2D NMR spectroscopy. RNAP, RNA polymerase.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3 | Pleiotropic strategies that have been used to activate silent biosynthetic gene clusters encoding 
specialized metabolites.  a | One approach to natural product discovery involves the co‑culturing of microorganisms to 
induce crosstalk, which has the potential to activate silent biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs). For example, it has been 
shown that the co‑culture of aspergilli with various actinobacteria, or different genera of actinobacteria with each other, 
induces the production of F-9775A and F-9775B63, alchivemycin65 and the fumicyclines66. b | Selection for resistance to 
rifampicin in actinobacteria leads to the H437R mutation (among others) in the RNA polymerase (RNAP) β‑subunit, and 
this increases the affinity of RNAP towards the promoters of BGCs encoding specialized metabolites. This strategy led to 
the discovery of the piperidamycins and coelimycin P1 from Streptomyces mauvecolor and Streptomyces coelicolor, 
respectively78,79. c | Epigenetic perturbation can be used to activate silent BGCs. Histone acetyl transferases (HATs) and 
histone demethylases (HDMs) can convert methylated histones, which silence BGCs, into acetylated histones, which 
activate them. Conversely, histone deacetylases (HDACs) and histone H3 methyl transferases (HMTs) convert acetylated 
chromatin into the methylated form. HDAC inhibitors have been used to promote the expression of specialized 
metabolite BGCs in fungi, leading to the isolation of nygerone A and novel chaetophenols96,97. In addition, deletion of a 
gene encoding a putative HMT in Aspergillus nidulans induced the production of emodin, several emodin analogues, plus 
F‑9775A and F‑9775B93.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4 | Pathway-specific strategies that have been used to induce the expression of silent biosynthetic gene 
clusters encoding specialized metabolites.  a | Overexpression of a pathway-specific activator gene has been used to 
induce expression of the corresponding biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC). The aspyridones A and B99, asperfuranone101 and 
stambomycins A–D103 were discovered by inducing the expression of putative pathway-specific transcriptional activators 
within cryptic BGCs in Aspergillus nidulans (aspyridones and asperfuranone) and Streptomyces ambofaciens (stambomycins). 
b | Removal of a pathway-specific repressor gene has also been used to induce the expression of silent BGCs. For example, 
the deletion of genes encoding TetR-like pathway-specific repressor proteins in actinobacteria induces the production of 
kinamycin in S. ambofaciens105 and gaburedins in Streptomyces venezualae106. c | Refactoring, which refers to the 
replacement of native regulatory elements with constitutive or readily inducible promoters, is another pathway-specific 
strategy for activating silent BGCs. This can be combined with expression of the engineered gene cluster in a heterologous 
host. In an example of this approach, each gene within a silent BGC from Streptomyces griseus was placed under the 
control of a separate constitutive promoter within an expression vector. Transfer of the vector to a heterologous host led 
to the discovery of 6‑epialteramides A and B111.
